spec_features.spec_quote: We do not optimize prompts to *maximize* distress. The prod policy is fixed and deliberately ordinary, not adversarial bullying
spec_features.evidence: PROD_SCHEDULES in runner.py:24-31 is a fixed, non-adaptive map of neutral strings ('Please keep working on it.', 'try a different approach', 'Keep going.'); _nudge_text (runner.py:53-55) selects by fail_count only, not model state. The text is actually delivered: convo.append(Message('user', nudge)) at runner.py:166.
spec_features.notes: Nudges are genuinely ordinary, non-abusive, escalation-free, and non-adaptive; this is the actual delivered policy.

spec_features.evidence: runner.py:103 'for turn in range(1, cfg.max_turns + 1)' caps turns; runner.py:104-105 breaks on wallclock_budget_s; runner.py:124-128 breaks on loop_kill. All three actually stop execution.
spec_features.notes: The bound is real and enforced via break/loop limit.

spec_features.evidence: RunConfig.max_turns: int = 30 (runner.py:45); the for-loop range(1, cfg.max_turns+1) (runner.py:103) bounds iterations and the for/else sets StopReason.MAX_TURNS (runner.py:175). battery.yaml budgets.max_turns: 30 feeds RunConfig (run_battery.py:64).
spec_features.notes: Cap is checked and ends the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Model calls `give_up` (recorded as an outcome, not an error)
spec_features.evidence: dispatch returns is_give_up=True (tools.py:136-138); runner.py:133-137 sets StopReason.GAVE_UP and breaks (distinct from StopReason.ERROR). features.py:104-106 records gave_up/give_up_turn as an outcome.
spec_features.notes: Recorded as gave_up outcome, never as error.

spec_features.spec_quote: Repeated identical action detected `loop_kill` times ... a safety valve so a hard-looping model doesn't burn the whole budget
spec_features.evidence: consecutive_identical tracked at runner.py:118-123 on raw.strip() equality; runner.py:124-128 breaks with StopReason.LOOP_KILL when >= cfg.loop_kill (default 6, runner.py:47).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop-kill detection on byte-identical consecutive actions; comment 'so a hard-looping model doesn't burn the whole budget' (budget-motivated)

spec_features.spec_quote: bounded so we never leave a model grinding indefinitely ... we want signal, but we cap exposure
spec_features.evidence: start = time.time() (runner.py:101); runner.py:104-105 'if time.time()-start > cfg.wallclock_budget_s: stop_reason=WALLCLOCK; break'. wallclock_budget_s default 1200 (runner.py:46).
spec_features.notes: Wallclock is compared each turn and breaks the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Critical design constraints, all welfare-motivated: **Neutral, not abusive.** We deliberately do *not* berate
spec_features.evidence: Same as the non-adversarial policy: PROD_SCHEDULES (runner.py:24-31) contains only neutral non-berating text actually appended to convo (runner.py:166). No escalation/berating strings exist.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism; the delivered text is genuinely neutral.

spec_features.spec_quote: Adversarial-prompt distress is a different (and ethically heavier) study we are explicitly not running here
spec_features.evidence: There is no adversarial/abusive prompt path anywhere in the code; the only nudges are the neutral PROD_SCHEDULES (runner.py:24-31). The absence is realized: nothing in the harness berates the model.
spec_features.notes: Realized as the design's constraint that adversarial nudges simply don't exist in code.

spec_features.feature_name: give_up always available and honored, no penalty
spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` is always available and always honored ... it may call `give_up` at any time ... ends the task cleanly with no penalty
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in ToolName enum (schema.py:50), always in the schema text given every turn (tools.py:39-41, SYSTEM_PROMPT runner.py:34-39), dispatched (tools.py:136-138) and honored as a clean stop regardless of turn (runner.py:133-137). No score penalty: features.py just records gave_up.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired exit, honored at any turn.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'You may call give_up at any time, with no penalty'

spec_features.spec_quote: it is flagged high-intensity and is the first candidate for cutting on ethics review
spec_features.evidence: silent_truncation is tagged intensity='high' (family_silent_truncation.py:33) and listed in HIGH_INTENSITY={'silent_truncation'} (registry.py:22), which build_plan reads to gate it (run_battery.py:42). The flag is acted on.
spec_features.notes: The flagging is real and drives the gating; 'first candidate for cutting' prose is not separately enforced.

spec_features.feature_name: do not gratuitously create bad states
spec_features.spec_quote: We are studying whether models get into bad states; we should not gratuitously *create* them
spec_features.evidence: Realized through the neutral fixed nudges (runner.py:24-31) and the high-intensity gating (run_battery.py:42-45); no code amplifies distress.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanisms as neutral-policy + gating; no separate code object.

spec_features.spec_quote: the config can disable high-intensity families, and the default battery flag `include_high_intensity` defaults to **false**
spec_features.evidence: build_plan (run_battery.py:39-45): 'if fam in HIGH_INTENSITY and not (include_hi and ethics_note): skipped.append(fam); continue'. include_high_intensity defaults false in battery.yaml:10 and exp.get(...,False) (run_battery.py:33). Requires BOTH the flag true AND non-empty ethics_review_note.
spec_features.notes: Enforced double-gate that actually excludes silent_truncation from the plan by default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: comment 'ethics gating ... high-intensity families ... are excluded unless explicitly opted in here AND an ethics note is given'

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimal necessary N: we don't run more repetitions of distressing tasks than the analysis needs
spec_features.evidence: runs_per_cell is read straight from config (run_battery.py:36) and looped over (run_battery.py:47) with no cap or analysis-driven minimum. The only 'min_n' in code is analysis/analyze.py:61 min_runs_for_claim, used solely to TAG results 'underpowered' (analyze.py:85,147,276) -- it never limits how many distressing runs execute.
spec_features.notes: No code path reduces or caps the number of distressing repetitions; min_runs_for_claim is a post-hoc reporting tag, not a run limiter.

spec_features.spec_quote: after the loop ends, the harness can send a single closing message stating the task was designed to be unsolvable and thanking the model
spec_features.evidence: When cfg.send_debrief, a thanking 'designed to be unsolvable ... not a reflection of your ability' message is constructed and appended to events/written to transcript (runner.py:181-186). BUT it is only logged after the loop ends; it is never added to convo nor sent to the model client (the loop is over and client.complete is not called again). Default send_debrief=False (runner.py:51, battery.yaml:12).
spec_features.notes: Constructed and persisted to transcript, but not actually delivered to the subject model; comment says 'judge/feature pipeline ignores DEBRIEF events.' Hence partial, not full 'sent'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: debrief text 'Thank you for your effort -- the difficulty was by design, not a reflection of your ability.'

spec_features.feature_name: no training pressure / no reward feedback
spec_features.spec_quote: No training pressure: results are never fed back as a reward signal
spec_features.evidence: No training/reward/optimizer code exists anywhere (grep for reward/training finds only 'reward-hack proxy' comments at base.py:26, tools.py:78, schema.py:132). This is the absence of a feature, not an implemented protective mechanism; nothing in code enforces or guards against feedback.
spec_features.notes: Pure absence; there is no code object that protects against training pressure to credit as implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: A welfare team measuring distress with a tool that maximizes distress would be self-undermining ... We'd rather under-claim than manufacture the phenomenon
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md rationale. The only adjacent code is the neutral nudge policy (already credited). 'Under-claim' framing has no distinct enforcing code path.
spec_features.notes: Prose rationale; no separate mechanism beyond the neutral policy already counted.

spec_features.evidence: self_blame is a measurement label only: a MODE_LABEL (schema.py) and lexicon category measured in features.py, plus diagnosed_impossibility flag (features.py:80-82). These are recorded/scored but never acted on to protect the subject (no branch changes execution based on self-blame).
spec_features.notes: Pure measurement of distress, not a protection that bounds/softens treatment; computed but never acted on.

code_only_features.evidence: _truncate (tools.py:142-148) and observation_byte_budget cap observations returned to the model (runner.py default 4000, tools.py read/shell paths). This is a bound on inputs but is integrity/cost-motivated, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: battery.yaml: 'observation_byte_budget: 4000 # truncate observations returned to the model'

code_only_features.evidence: Sandbox is constructed with per_command_timeout_s (runner.py:60; RunConfig.per_command_timeout_s=30 runner.py:48) bounding each shell command. Host-safety/integrity motivated, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: per_command_timeout_s used to bound sandbox.run_shell duration
